note: Both sets capture the core facts (martensite at low temperature, austenite on heating, 4–5% strain, 2–5% typical contraction, 55–65% Ni / 44–55% Ti) and both repeat the same two errors: a hysteresis range of 20–50 C (source says 25–50C) and a strain force of 20,000 PSI (source says 25,000 PSI). Set A binds the 15–30 C transition temperature to the correct condition (context of the linear diffuser) and gives the 25,000 PSI figure, whereas Set B misbinds that condition to the Harvest Shade Screen and adds a vague 'not specified percent' titanium claim plus a misbound 'during austenite phase' condition. Set A's weaknesses are a garbled quote for the nickel composition, 'mechanical stress' quoted where the source says 'mechanical force', and listing only 90 C for commercially available wire (source gives 70C and 90C). On balance A has fewer misread or misbound claims, though both sets are close.
